newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schmidhuber urges IGC to make notable progress.
newsitem.headline: Schmidhuber urges IGC to make notable progress.

text.p: European governments must show notable progress in further European integration or risk losing the support of the general public for the integration process, Bundesbank board member Peter Schmidhuber said on Friday.

In a speech to be delivered to a German-Dutch conference in Ebenhausen, in the state of Bavaria, Schmidhuber said it would be critical for the so-called Intergovernmental Conference (IGC, a year-long meeting of European Union government officials, to show some progress in this area.
"The European Council meeting in Amsterdam in June 1997 should reach fundamental decisions regarding the IGC or even complete it," Schmidhuber said in the text of a speech.
"One can only hope that the Dutch presidency will suceed in achieving a respectable result," he added.
The IGC is intended to address political issues related to further European integration as well as to set the blueprint for the admission of additional states to the 15-nation group.
"If we find ourselves empty-handed after Amsterdam, or even after (the December summit in) Luxembourg, this would have disadvantageous consequences for the realisation of Stage Three," he said.
He listed two possible such consequences.
"The drive for political integration within the general public -- in so far as such a thing exists -- would ebb away further," Schmidhuber said.
He added "the question would also then need to be asked as to whether the lack of progress on integration disturbs the basis for economic and monetary union."
